name: Beijing Street Perception: Six Scales from 0 to 10
description:
Method replication: participants look at each of 24 Beijing street views for at least 10 seconds, then rate how beautiful, boring, depressing, lively, safe and wealthy the place is, each from 0 to 10; the images are not the paper's stimuli (99 newly fetched Baidu street views inside the Sixth Ring Road, one direction per point, 2018 or later).

Original study: Jin, Li, Zhou, Li, Raxidin & Zhang (2026), Environment, Development and Sustainability. From 16,379 Baidu sampling points every 100 m along main roads inside Beijing's Sixth Ring Road (four directions, 512 × 256 px), 120 points were drawn from each ring zone, giving 2,880 images split into 30 groups of 96. 30 participants aged 20–24 (15 men, 15 women), after one hour of training, viewed each image for 10 s on a Tobii Pro Fusion eye tracker and then had 15 s to rate it on the six Place Pulse 2.0 dimensions on a 0–10 scale. Ratings and gaze features trained a multimodal model that mapped the six perceptions across the city.

Differences from the original study: (1) no eye tracking and no training session; (2) 24 images per participant instead of 96, drawn at random rather than by ring zone; (3) the end labels "0 = not at all" and "10 = extremely" are written for this template; (4) no 15-second limit on rating.
author: Jin, Li, Zhou, Li, Raxidin & Zhang
